clue.text: State of the art — an impediment without direction

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the snag wraps round the compass point

parts.note: a hitch is a snag or impediment
E, east, is a compass direction

explanation.surface: Being cutting-edge is held back by an obstacle with no clear way forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, not lacking: HITCH goes round E to give HITECH.
explanation.definitionFit: Hi-tech equipment uses the most advanced technology, the current state of the art.

clue.text: In muddled head reminder turns up to get Mother's Pride?

indicators.note: in places the turned note within the jumbled letters
muddled shows the word head is jumbled
turns up reverses the note in a down entry

parts.note: a memo is a reminder

explanation.surface: A confused mind finds a note that leads to a famous loaf brand.
explanation.walkthrough: Mother's Pride is a British sliced-bread brand; the question mark signals that the setter means what a mother is proud of baking herself.
explanation.definitionFit: Homemade food is what a mother takes pride in, playing on a bread brand name.

clue.text: Everyone in the race gets a drink, which is hard to believe

indicators.note: in puts everyone inside the race

parts.note: the TT is the Isle of Man motorcycle race
all means everyone
ale is a drink

explanation.surface: All the competitors get a drink at the race, an unlikely story.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall tale is an exaggerated story that strains credibility.

clue.text: Animal of Romanic or Gipsy stock?

indicators.note: stock suggests the letters are drawn from the lineage of these words

explanation.surface: Is this creature of Romance or Romany descent?
explanation.definitionFit: A corgi is a small breed of dog, so an animal.

clue.text: Politician in winter sport is being mean

indicators.note: in tells us the politician sits inside the sport

parts.note: skiing is a winter sport
MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician

explanation.surface: A politician on the ski slopes is accused of stinginess.
explanation.definitionFit: Skimping is economising meanly, giving too little.

clue.text: Philosopher covers nocturnal sin by gallants of old

indicators.note: covers puts the philosopher round the other pieces

parts.note: Kant was a German philosopher
night's means of the night, nocturnal
to err is to sin

explanation.surface: A thinker conceals a night-time misdeed committed by old-fashioned suitors.
explanation.definitionFit: Knights errant were medieval wandering knights, chivalrous gallants of the past.

clue.text: English student managed somehow to get to college

indicators.note: somehow signals the letters arrive in some new order

parts.note: L is a learner driver, a student

explanation.surface: An English student somehow got into university.
explanation.definitionFit: Magdalene is one of the colleges of Cambridge University.

clue.text: Setter's about to stay in the same place

indicators.note: about puts the setter's words round the waiting verb

parts.note: the setter's is I'm, the setter is I
to bide is to stay

explanation.surface: The puzzle compiler is going to remain where he is.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibidem is Latin for 'in the same place', used in footnotes.

clue.text: Entry to the French is a piece of cake

parts.note: a gate is an entry
au is French for to the

explanation.surface: Getting into the French is easy.
explanation.definitionFit: A gateau is a rich layered cake, served by the slice.

clue.text: Moral degeneration in the mouth

indicators.note: degeneration suggests the word moral falling apart and reforming

explanation.surface: Moral decay shows in what someone says.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: a back tooth is something found in the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: A grinding back tooth is located in the mouth.

clue.text: The in thing is outrageous size — get it?

indicators.note: outrageous suggests the letters running wild into a new order

explanation.surface: A fashion for enormous size is mocked: do you see the joke?
explanation.definitionFit: The spirit of the age is whatever is currently fashionable, the in thing.

clue.text: Accepting nothing

parts.note: a policy that accepts no misbehaviour at all, read as accepting a nought

explanation.definitionFit: A policy of strict enforcement tolerates no offences whatsoever.

clue.text: Domineering lady has a short trip during the month …

indicators.note: during places the short journey inside the month

parts.note: March is a month

indicators.note: short means the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: a trip is a journey

explanation.surface: A bossy woman takes a brief holiday in the course of the month.
explanation.definitionFit: A matriarch is a woman who rules a family, often in a commanding way.

clue.text: … where it all happens over a long period

indicators.note: over signals turning the phrase back to front

parts.note: an era is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: the place where everything has taken place for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue to the one before, but the parse stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is the scene of action, the place where events play out.

clue.text: One directed back to German city eating cat food

indicators.note: eating puts the cat inside the combined letters
back reverses the words one and directed together

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral
led means directed
Essen is a city in Germany's Ruhr

explanation.surface: Someone is sent back to a German city where they eat cat meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the words for one and directed together; 'eating' then opens the run of shop and city to admit the pet.
explanation.definitionFit: A delicatessen is a shop selling prepared foods, and the word also covers the foods themselves.

clue.text: Like the hordes who don't matter so much?

definitions.meaning: hordes are too many to number
read as counting less, being less important

explanation.definitionFit: Countless means innumerable; split, it says one counts for less.

clue.text: Satisfied with a quantity of fuel

definitions.meaning: read as a grate full of coal

explanation.definitionFit: Grateful means thankful; split, it is the amount a fireplace holds.

clue.text: Squeal about wine being execrable

indicators.note: about puts the singing round the wine

parts.note: to sing is to squeal, to inform
hock is German white wine

explanation.surface: An informer around wine is behaving appallingly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Squeal' and 'sing' both mean inform to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Shocking means dreadful or very bad, as is execrable.

clue.text: Arthur feels Lancelot initially refined oil cleaner

indicators.note: refined suggests the letters being processed into a new form
initially takes the opening letter of Lancelot

explanation.surface: King Arthur senses that Lancelot is a polished gentleman.
explanation.definitionFit: Fuller's earth is an absorbent clay used to soak up grease and oil.

clue.text: Aura of game on public transport

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the game above the vehicle

parts.note: nim is a matchstick game
a bus is public transport

explanation.surface: A halo seen during a game on the bus.
explanation.definitionFit: A nimbus is a halo or luminous aura around a holy figure.

clue.text: One suffers with two lads

parts.note: Vic is a boy's name
Tim is a boy's name

explanation.surface: Someone is in pain alongside a couple of boys.
explanation.definitionFit: A victim is a person who suffers harm.

clue.text: State one returns to as a fool

parts.note: ID is the abbreviation for Idaho, a US state
one is I, the Roman numeral

indicators.note: returns turns the little word to round

explanation.surface: A country to which someone comes back, playing the fool.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiot is a stupid person, a fool.

clue.text: It is clear and could be true to life

indicators.note: could be hints that the letters may form something else

explanation.surface: It's obvious and might well be the case.
explanation.definitionFit: Realistic means representing things as they really are.

clue.text: A doctor within two feet

indicators.note: within puts the letter and doctor inside the numeral

parts.note: II is two in Roman numerals
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor

explanation.surface: A medic stands between two legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Iambi are metrical feet of a short syllable then a long one.

clue.text: Goat head, a sort of pumpkin down under

definitions.text: a sort of pumpkin down under

parts.note: a goat is a butter, an animal that butts
nut is slang for the head

explanation.surface: A goat's head is like an Australian pumpkin.
explanation.walkthrough: BUTTER here is one who butts, not the dairy spread. In Australia butternut squash is called butternut pumpkin.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australia and New Zealand the butternut squash is known as a pumpkin variety.

clue.text: Church ladies' outfit to wear off duty

annotationWithheld.clue: Church ladies' outfit to wear off duty

clue.text: Term sees alternative terminology across the pond …

indicators.note: alternative suggests another arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: Term sees different vocabulary used in America.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on to the next clue, which also uses American words.
explanation.definitionFit: In American colleges a half-year teaching period is the usual word for a term.

clue.text: … where help turns to record Obama's conversation

indicators.note: turns tells us to read the word for help backwards

parts.note: aid means help
a log is a written record

explanation.surface: Continuing on: where assistance is used to log an American president's talk.
explanation.walkthrough: Obama signals the American spelling, without the final -UE.
explanation.definitionFit: Dialog is the American spelling of a conversation between people.
